questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to study somwhere were english is the native language for the locals. Furthermore, I always dreamed about living in australia, and saw this as the perfect opportunity to include it in my studies

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: From KU side, it was in the beginning well organised, however after i got accapted it took severeal month until i recieved further information which was a bit annoying. However, once we got in contact with our supervisor in Sydney everyting went super smooth and she answered my emails super quickly and well organized.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I got picked up with a shuttle service from my dorm which already smoothened the arrival with jetlag in sydney. A few days afterwards we had our first introduction day with our coordinator which was really helpfull to hear all the most important things again that we have to concider.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I recieved an email from USYD about housing information. I had to instantly apply for housing. Its called "guranteed" housing, even though this might mean that you get the most expensive accommodation. I was lucky and got a spot in Scape city central, where you share your room but otherwise live in a shared apartment with other 7 people. I really enjoyed my time there. Its between the CBD and campus. Supermarkets are only 2min by walking distance away. If you are a social person who doenst mind to share a room (which has still a lot of privacy) I can definetly recommend to stay there. Be quick with the applications in teh esecond you recieve te email from USYD regarding housing.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: all accommodations are expensive. I really enjoyed living close to campus as so many classes are mandatory and tehrefore a big pat of my life tehre also played on campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: we recieved a list of all possible classes from our coordinator. That was really helpfull. If i was in slightest doubt I was able to easyly contact her. also after i arrived in sydney.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
I informed myself about possible exchange destinations within my masters degree. While i found USYD i alredy checked which classes they broadly offer, so i would know if i can find classes that are within my study area and also actually interest me. 
The application afterwards was pretty mooth. As far as i rememebr i had to provide a list of my preferred universities. and write a motivation letter for my first choiice. after a few i recieved the accaptence from KU.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Online portal from KU

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I recieved all the classes that i hoepd for

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Inform yourself a lot and dont hesitate to contact your coordinator there. they aremore then helpfull.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: In my opinion the level of the classes was similar to teh ones at KU. Just a few of the economics classes had a higher intensity i would say. But I guess taht also really depends on teh teaching style of the professor and how well you can learn from him/her.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: At KU i am used to small cassroom sizes and interactive classes. at usyd the classe are wa bigger and hence its not as interactive. The mandatory classes were for me also new, which i not necessarily liked that much. But they are still managable, and mostly ou have 1-2 days off if you choose classes wisely and look on their potential scheduele from te last years.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Market Structure and strategic behaviour
dynamics of economic change
energy and teh environent
food and water security

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I really enjoyed the Energy and environmnet class. teh topics were really interesting, even though the professor was maybe not the smoothest. Furthermore  really liked the dynamics of ecoonomic change class which gave me a good insight into australian regulations.

questions.answer: Eggs and beers are way more expensive than in denmark

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: i joyned the bushwalkers society who go on several hiked in sydney region. Also teh yoga society

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend the above mentioned, because i really enjoyed them and it was nice to meet people, also locals. In general just look into the whole list of societies and try anything that sounds interesting. However, towards teh middle of the semester when you meet friends and maybe plan trips, I at leats did not have that much time anymore to partcipiate in these socities.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Tasmania, Melbourne, East Coast and definetly West coast (perth to Exmouth)! The east coast everyone travels which is also really beautiful but for me WA was definetly the highlight. It really reprenets the true wild Australia.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I had no issues wit adapting.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: If you are in your MAsters degree its more difficult to meet Aussies, as most of them only do their bachelors. so dont count on meeting aussies in your classes. Go out, join the societies or local run clubs. And just be open minded as the aussies are all super chill and talktive.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I wouldnt say that tehre are any specif cultural challanges. Just try to be yourself and dont worry about the english language.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: That everyone is so open mided, talktive and just relaxed. They are suoer welcoming and heartwarming.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Inform youself well about the classes you can take.
Be yourself and enjoy the aussie lifestyle! Wake up early as they do and start the day.
Take any chance you get.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: no

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: To meet such amazing new friends and share all the moments within sydney and on trips togetehr with them. They become quickly your second famiily.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: To not travel too much :)) and still get the classes done

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
